props.title: Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street
props.initialSlug: Murderous barber serves bloody revenge in London

sections.content: Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street (2007) represents Tim Burton's darkest musical adaptation, transforming Stephen Sondheim's Broadway masterpiece into a blood-soaked Gothic nightmare. Johnny Depp's vengeful barber follows the grand tradition of tragic horror antiheroes like Erik from The Phantom of the Opera (2004) and The Count of Monte Cristo (2002), but with a macabre twist that aligns more closely with Burton's signature style seen in Sleepy Hollow (1999). The film's desaturated color palette, broken only by shocking crimson spurts, creates a Victorian London as oppressive as the one in From Hell (2001).

sections.content: Helena Bonham Carter's Mrs. Lovett provides the film's black humor, turning murder into meat pies in a twisted take on female entrepreneurship that echoes Little Shop of Horrors (1986). The film's practical effects and minimal CGI create visceral horror moments that harken back to classic Hammer horror films like Horror of Dracula (1958), while Sondheim's complex score maintains its theatrical power through Burton's cinematic lens. SUBHEAD: Musical Horror Innovation

Sweeney Todd (2007) opened new possibilities for horror musicals, influencing later works like Repo! The Genetic Opera (2008) and Anna and the Apocalypse (2017). Burton's decision to cast actors who weren't primarily singers - but could convey deep emotional trauma - prioritized the dark dramatic elements over pure vocal virtuosity. This approach influenced later musical adaptations like Into the Woods (2014), where the focus remained on character interpretation over traditional musical theater performance.
